aggregate_initial_judgment: Read before opening seat totals. Claim: an MCP<->ROS2 middleware that derives typed agent tools from ROS message schemas, offers a direct path and a persistent perception-inference-control (PIC) path under explicit lifecycle tools, and confines VLA backend/runtime/acceleration changes to a fixed inference boundary, enabling modular orchestration and backend switching without rewiring. Evidence: Cases I-III are qualitative figures (multi-platform base control and single arm in simulation, one FR3 grasp sequence) with no counts and no LLM-agent task success; Case IV runs OpenVLA-OFT FastV pruning presets on LIBERO (500 episodes/suite) under the fixed topology and an OpenVLA latency figure whose values are not in the text. Nothing measures integration effort, reuse, or the middleware against hand-written wrappers or other MCP-ROS bridges. Expected: system_method infrastructure, online only via the VLA-in-middleware LIBERO runs, scoped support, weak E.measurement/E.causality.

gap.author_gap: Agent tool APIs and robot middleware are mismatched; ad-hoc wrappers drift and must be redone when VLA backends or serving stacks change.
gap.checked_gap: A real engineering seam with named neighbours (ROS2mcpserver, ROS2mcp, RynnRCP, RoboOS) and a specific residue claim (schema derivation, lifecycle-aware execution, reuse across execution patterns). candidate_checks.reason: Full cards read. The parent replaces bespoke per-modality pipelines with one uniform model over a shared representation/objective, and its success conditions concern representation compatibility and a uniform objective. RoboNeuron standardises a call surface: robot-side controllers and VLA backends stay separate; no model is trained or unified. C18's serializer step is the closest analogue but its load-bearing claim (a recipe transferring unchanged, validated by ablation against a naive baseline) has no counterpart. son55 itself rated the fit 'weak' with steps 4-5 unmet; per PATTERN_PROTOCOL a weak terminology-level fit is not assigned.
The middleware does not decompose a task; an external agent would. No solver-verdict loop.

G.reason: sol adopted (son55 2). The gap is specific (schema drift, unmanaged long-running loops, backend re-integration), the neighbours are named with the precise capability each lacks (agg:D08), and the residue is bounded (topic-level only). Not 4: the bottleneck's cost is unsourced and the neighbours' deficits are asserted, not checked. son55's main objection (no side-by-side comparison) is an evidence question judged under E.causality.

M.reason: sol adopted (son55 2). Each mechanism answers its problem by construction (schema derivation -> no wrapper drift; fixed I/O contract -> swaps without rewiring) and makes a checkable prediction (topology unchanged across presets), contrary to son55's 'no distinguishable prediction'. Key assumption is weak: one 6-DoF delta + gripper contract (agg:D06) must fit every VLA backend; tool naming/descriptions for LLM selection not considered.
